chapter: Front matter — List of Figures / List of Tables (vs Ch. 3)
evidence: List of Figures (PDF p.9): "3.4 Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior . . . 57". List of Tables (PDF p.11): "Table 3-3 Parameter, compute and KV accounting for two model scales: dense 70B (canonical 80L/8192H full-MHA geometry) vs MoE 8×7B class (~47B total, its own 32L/4096H GQA geometry) . . . 58", with the note "where a caption closes one page and the rows begin on a later one — Table 3-3 is that case in this edition — the folio follows the rows, not the caption." In the body, the Fig. 3.4 art and its caption "figure 3.4: Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior." are on folio 56 (PDF p.80); the Table 3-3 caption closes folio 55 (PDF p.79); the table's header row "metric | dense 70B | MoE (8×7B class) | derivation" begins on folio 57 (PDF p.81). Body folio = PDF page − 24 (verified at Fig. 1.1/folio 10, Fig. 3.1/folio 41, Table 4-2 rows/folio 81, Part III title/folio 141).
issue: Both front-matter folios for this one stretch are stale: Fig. 3.4 is listed at 57 but sits on folio 56, and Table 3-3 is listed at 58, which matches neither its caption folio (55) nor the folio where its rows begin (57) — the book's own stated rows-folio rule yields 57. The List-of-Tables note is also inaccurate: it names Table 3-3 as *the* caption-closes-a-page/rows-begin-later case, but Table 3-1 (caption folio 43, rows folio 44) and Table 4-2 (caption folio 80, rows folio 81) are the same situation. Every neighbouring entry checked (Tables 1-1, 2-1, 2-2, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 5-1, 5-2, 6-1, 7-1 and Figs. 1.1–6.2) matches the body, so the error is localised but will send a reader to the wrong pages.
fix_instruction: Regenerate the front-matter figure/table folios from the rebuilt PDF: Fig. 3.4 → p. 56, Table 3-3 → p. 57 (rows folio), and re-word the List-of-Tables note so it does not single out Table 3-3 as the unique caption/rows split.

evidence: Preface (PDF p.22): "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A" — but the same page also says "Appendix A, A.6 carries a boxed 2026-09-27 capability probe" and "a superseding re-verification of the DeepSeek model-service status (Appendix A, A.3)"; Ch. 4 Table 4-2 note (PDF p.75): "Appendix A's §A.7 (Fig A.2, vendor-relative KV/compute ratios)"; Ch. 1 (PDF p.27): "all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10"; Ch. 3 (PDF p.76): "model card HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, accessed 2026-08-30; A.10".
issue: Three mutually inconsistent reference forms are used for one class of target — Appendix A's own section numbers: "§ 9A" (number-then-letter, which the Preface defines as the scheme), "A.3 / A.6 / A.7 / A.10" (letter-then-number) and a bare "§10". Under the convention the Preface states, "§10" and "A.10" do not resolve to a "9A"-style label, and a reader cannot tell whether they name the same section. The same prefix is also used for figure numbers ("Fig A.2") and section numbers ("§A.7"), which compounds the ambiguity. This is a cross-reference defect that will not resolve for a reader navigating Appendix A.
fix_instruction: Choose one appendix-section label scheme (e.g. "§ A.10", "§ A.7") and normalise every occurrence to it — including the Preface's definition of "§ 9A" and the bare "§10" in Ch. 1 — or, if "9A" is a genuinely distinct subsection label, print the full scheme (section number + subsection letter) once in the Preface and map the A.N references onto it.

chapter: Ch. 5 — From Workload to Model Selection
evidence: In-text references use the letter form: PDF p.111 "the quality claim itself is the §5.3(a)/§5.7 item still to validate on the target corpus"; PDF p.113 "Read them with the reconciliation note in §5.3(b) before comparing them with Ch 4's input-token per-dollar figures"; PDF p.122 "the §5.3(a) ~15% MAP uplift"; PDF p.118 "the parametric Q∗ in §5.3 shows how to decide". The chapter's own headings are numerically numbered with the letters only as decoration: "5.3.1. (a) Embedding-model selection for the retrieval leg", "5.3.2. (b) Generation-model selection for the answer leg", "5.3.3. (c) Base-model + RAG + guardrails vs fine-tuned model". The Preface fixes the rule: "A section reference takes the form § N.M ... so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4".
issue: Chapter 5's cross-references point at subsections using "§5.3(a)/(b)/(c)", a numbering form that does not exist in the scheme the book declares and uses elsewhere (there is no subsection 5.3(a); the targets are 5.3.1–5.3.3). Under the book's own convention these references are unresolvable, and one of them ("the parametric Q∗ in §5.3") points to a whole section when the target is §5.3.3 — a third form of the same reference.
fix_instruction: Normalise Ch. 5's internal references to §5.3.1 / §5.3.2 / §5.3.3 (and change "the parametric Q∗ in §5.3" to §5.3.3), or renumber the headings themselves to carry the letters as identifiers; then apply a global sweep for other "§N.M(x)" forms.

chapter: Ch. 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
evidence: PDF p.96: "Time basis: this is the rate over the active business-hours window (an 8-hour × 260-workday schedule), not 24×7 wall-clock." Three lines later, the same page: "Over 24×7 the same 10 rps would extrapolate to ~18.7M requests/month on the same 260-workday calendar (10 × 3,600 × 24 × 260/12 = 18,720,000) — 3× the active-hours volume — or ~9,360 requests/user/month for 2,000 users".
issue: The same quantity is labelled "not 24×7 wall-clock" and then "Over 24×7". The parenthetical arithmetic is 24 hours per *workday* on a 260-workday calendar (520 h/mo), i.e. 18.72M requests/month; a true 24×7 basis on a 730-hour month is 10 × 3,600 × 730 = 26,280,000 (~26.28M requests/month), ~40% higher. The label therefore misdescribes the basis it is attached to, in a paragraph whose whole purpose is to prevent an hour-basis mismatch — the same class of error the book flags elsewhere (e.g. the 730-hour vs 173.33-active-hour spend mismatch).
fix_instruction: Rename the case to what it is — "24 hours a day on the same 260-workday calendar" (or "all wall-clock hours on workdays") — and, if a genuine 24×7 comparison is wanted, add it separately as ~26.28M requests/month (10 × 3,600 × 730).
